nodes.label: Elias in the Lighthouse, Again? Diagnosing Low Diversity in LLM Stories
nodes.author: Sil Hamilton, David Mimno
nodes.rationale: Empirical study of mode collapse in LLM-generated stories: 88.3% contain 11 core tokens (Elias, lighthouse, keeper) at rates 900× higher than published literature.

nodes.label: Mode Collapse in Creative Writing
nodes.rationale: LLM-generated stories show homogeneous output across model families; 20,000 stories from four models (Claude, Gemini, GPT, OLMo) with five prompts each.

nodes.label: Core Vocabulary Analysis
nodes.rationale: 11 core tokens identified via changepoint analysis: names (Elias 26.5%, Mara 16.7%, Elara 13.1%), professions (keeper 48.1%), location (lighthouse 51.2%).

nodes.label: Training Data Source Analysis
nodes.rationale: Core tokens not explained by pre-training or post-training data prevalence; 3,053 of 78,958 OLMo post-training stories contain core tokens (3.8%), yet 88.3% of generated stories do.

nodes.label: Alignment-Driven Mode Collapse Hypothesis
nodes.rationale: Speculative: models trained to avoid copyrighted characters and adult content during alignment; DPO and RL stages show 5–8× higher core density than SFT despite being 80% of post-training stories.
